title: Overpacking Is Travelers' Biggest Mistake
paragraphs: Do you always take too many things on vacation? If so, you are not alone. According to a new survey, overpacking is still the biggest mistake that experienced travelers make.

The survey was carried out by Global Rescue, a company that provides travel security and emergency services, between June 30 and July 6, 2026. It asked experienced international travelers about their travel mistakes and their favorite travel tips.

The results showed that 38% of travelers said that taking too much luggage was their biggest travel mistake. This number was up from 32% in 2025. However, it is much lower than in February 2020, just before the COVID-19 pandemic, when 74% of travelers said overpacking was their biggest mistake. Overpacking has been the top mistake every year.

Other common mistakes were booking flights with very little time to change planes, at 19%, planning too many activities with no extra time, at 10%, and traveling without offline maps or digital copies of booking documents, at 8%. Another 8% said their biggest mistake was changing money at expensive airport counters.

Dan Richards, the head of Global Rescue, said, "Overpacking is the single most consistent preventable mistake we see, year after year." According to Richards, heavy bags can make travelers tired and increase the risk of falling and hurting their backs. In an emergency, travelers with heavy bags also move more slowly. "In a crisis, the ability to move quickly can be just as important as what you packed," he said.

The survey also asked about travelers' favorite travel hacks. The most popular one was putting a smart tag in checked luggage to track it, at 31%. Next came emailing copies of passports and IDs to themselves, at 16%. Other popular tips included using special packing cubes that make clothes smaller and rolling clothes instead of folding them.
